proof:
# Uniform endpoint credits near the middle-simplex facet directions

Historical claim of scope (pending review here): proved local directional theorem. The endpoint credits below are fixed numbers, independent of both the nearby continuous normal and the nearby middle-fiber point. They concern every integer tilt. No assertion about all other directions or the full OC conclusion is made.

Let \(d\ge1\), \(N=d+1\), \(j=\lceil N/2\rceil\), and \(b=1/N\). Let \(B,C\subset\mathbb R^d\) be simplices of equal volume \(V>0\), and let \(A\) be an arbitrary convex body of volume \(a>0\), satisfying

\[
                         (A+C)/2\subset B.                 \tag{1}
\]

Use either margin \(\delta=\delta_N\) or the larger \(\delta_N^*\) proved in `candidate 986ab1688d049a3b`. The property needed here is: for every \(p\in A\), at least \(j\) middle-simplex barycentric coordinates obey

\[
                  \lambda_i(p)+\max_C\lambda_i
                              \ge2b+2\delta.               \tag{2}
\]

In particular \(0<\delta<1\). Brunn–Minkowski gives \(a\le V\); set \(r=(a/V)^{1/d}\).

## 1. A uniformly bounded frame using permitted transformations

Apply an invertible continuous affine map sending \(B\) to the standard simplex
\(\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)\). All masses are multiplied by the same Jacobian, so \(a/V\) and all subsequent homogeneous mass inequalities are unchanged. Continue to write \(A,B,C,a,V\) for the transformed data.

Choose \(p_0\in A\), and apply the ambient shear

\[
                         (z,x)\longmapsto(z,x+zp_0).
\]

The three fibers become \(A-p_0,B,C+p_0\). They still satisfy (1), their volumes are unchanged, and the integer bases remain \(-1,0,1\). In this new frame, renamed again,

\[
                0\in A,\qquad C\subset2B,
                \qquad A\subset2(B-B).                   \tag{3}
\]

Indeed, \(0\in A\) and (1) imply \(C\subset2B\). Fix \(c_0\in C\). The same inclusion gives \(A+c_0\subset2B\), and \(c_0\in2B\), proving the last assertion. Consequently, with

\[
                             R=2\sqrt d,
\]

every point of \(A\cup C\cup B\) has norm at most \(R\). In particular, no diameter hypothesis on the small body \(A\) is being added.

The shear merely adds a fixed number to the integer tilt of each continuous normal. Thus a statement holding for every integer tilt is preserved. For barycentric coordinates, the changes in \(\lambda_i(p)\) and \(\max_C\lambda_i\) are opposite, so (2) is also preserved exactly.

All remaining formulas refer to this bounded standard-simplex frame. Their pullbacks give neighborhoods of the corresponding directions in the original coordinates; no Euclidean-affine invariance of a numerical angular radius is asserted.

## 2. Fixed measurable subsets with a multiplicity lower bound

Put \(h_i=\max_C\lambda_i\), and define

\[
 A_i=\{p\in A:\lambda_i(p)+h_i\ge2b+\delta\},
 \qquad c_i=|A_i|.                                        \tag{4}
\]

These are compact convex subsets, possibly empty or of zero volume. By (2), every point of \(A\) belongs to at least \(j\) of them. Hence

\[
               0\le c_i\le a,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^N c_i\ge ja.\tag{5}
\]

The margin in (4) is smaller than the guaranteed margin in (2). This leaves a fixed margin for both direction and center perturbations. No common set of \(j\) indices is required throughout \(A\).

## 3. Uniformity over all nearby normals, points, and integer tilts

Let \(y\in B\) obey

\[
                    \max_i(\lambda_i(y)-b)_+\le\sigma.
\]

For a fixed index \(i\), consider any affine functional

\[
                        f_i(x)=\lambda_i(x)+v\cdot x,
                        \qquad |v|\le\varepsilon.
\]

An arbitrary constant added to \(f_i\) cancels from all the following cuts. If

\[
                      2\sigma+2r+6R\varepsilon<\delta,     \tag{6}
\]

then for every real integer tilt \(\beta\),

\[
\boxed{
 |A\cap\{f_i\ge f_i(y)+\beta\}|+
 |C\cap\{f_i\ge f_i(y)-\beta\}|\ \ge c_i.
}                                                         \tag{7}
\]

Here and below the normal is taken nonzero. In particular it is nonzero under the explicit neighborhood sizes in (10).

To prove (7), write \(h(f)=\max_C f\) and \(W(f)=\max_C f-\min_C f\). The homothetic-cap argument from the fixed-facet theorem applies to every nonconstant affine \(f\), without requiring that its direction be a simplex facet normal. It gives

\[
 \inf_\beta\bigl[|A\cap\{f\ge f(y)+\beta\}|+
                  |C\cap\{f\ge f(y)-\beta\}|\bigr]
 \ge |A\cap\{f\ge 2f(y)-h(f)+W(f)r\}|.                   \tag{8}
\]

Indeed, the \(C\)-cap at \(h(f)-W(f)r\) contains a homothetic copy of \(C\) of volume \(a\). If the actual \(C\)-cap has smaller mass, its threshold is strictly larger, forcing the \(A\)-threshold strictly below the right-hand threshold in (8). Otherwise the \(C\)-cap alone pays at least \(a\).

For \(p\in A_i\), set \(\kappa=R\varepsilon\). The support bound (3), the definition (4), and \(W(\lambda_i)\le2\) give

\[
\begin{aligned}
 f_i(p)+h(f_i)&\ge2b+\delta-2\kappa,\\
 f_i(y)&\le b+\sigma+\kappa,\\
 W(f_i)&\le2+2\kappa.
\end{aligned}
\]

Consequently

\[
 f_i(p)+h(f_i)-2f_i(y)-W(f_i)r
 \ge\delta-2\sigma-2r-4\kappa-2\kappa r
 \ge\delta-2\sigma-2r-6\kappa>0.                           \tag{9}
\]

Thus \(A_i\) is contained in the set on the right of (8), proving (7). This works for the same \(c_i\) simultaneously for every allowed \(y,v,\beta\).

For example the explicit closed conditions

\[
 \boxed{\quad r\le\delta/8,\qquad \sigma\le\delta/8,
          \qquad\varepsilon\le\delta/(24R)\quad}           \tag{10}
\]

leave a gap of at least \(\delta/4\) in (9). Since every standard-simplex barycentric gradient has norm at least one, \(\varepsilon<1\) also guarantees a nonzero normal.

If \(n_i=\nabla\lambda_i\) and \(u_i=n_i/|n_i|\), the theorem includes all unit normals \(u\) satisfying

\[
                 |u-u_i|\le\frac{\delta}{24R\sqrt d}.
                                                               \tag{11}
\]

To see this, multiply the cap inequality by \(|n_i|>0\), and use \(v=|n_i|(u-u_i)\), with \(|n_i|\le\sqrt d\). Integer tilts are rescaled by the same positive factor and remain unrestricted. These are oriented neighborhoods of the vertex-side facet normals; the opposite directions are not silently included.

All inequalities concern closed ambient halfspaces. Nonvertical boundary hyperplanes have zero volume in every full-dimensional fiber. The proof uses actual subset inclusion even before discarding such boundaries. A halfspace containing \((0,y)\) whose boundary does not pass through it contains the parallel boundary-through-point halfspace, so its mass is no smaller.

## 4. Applicability to the proposed credit-dependent middle point

Let \(\gamma=\gamma_d\), \(\bar c=N^{-1}\sum_i c_i\), and define \(y\) by

\[
                \lambda_i(y)=b+\frac{c_i-\bar c}{N\gamma V}.
                                                               \tag{12}
\]

These numbers sum to one and obey

\[
      |\lambda_i(y)-b|\le\frac{a}{N\gamma V}.
\]

Thus, if \(a/V<\gamma\), they are all strictly positive and determine \(y\in\operatorname{int}B\). In addition, the sufficient hypotheses

\[
 \frac aV\le(\delta/8)^d,\qquad
 \frac aV\le N\gamma\delta/8,
 \qquad \frac aV<\gamma                                  \tag{13}
\]

ensure that this \(y\) meets (10). The credits in (4) are determined before choosing \(y\), so there is no fixed-point assumption.

Equation (7) therefore supplies these fixed endpoint credits throughout the oriented normal neighborhoods (11) at the point (12). Establishing the middle-simplex contribution and handling every direction outside those neighborhoods remain separate steps. No depth lower bound for the complete three-fiber measure is claimed in this note.

The exact elementary margin checks are recorded in `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_robust_simplex_endpoint_credit.py`.
